title: Turning points in world history
description: The handful of changes that shaped the world, with the dates to hang them on.

ideas.title: Farming and the first cities
ideas.summary: Farming let people settle, store a surplus, and build the first cities and writing systems along great rivers.

items.q: What name do historians give to the shift from hunting and gathering to farming, which began roughly 12,000 years ago?
Between which two rivers did the cities of ancient Mesopotamia arise?
Which wedge-shaped writing system was pressed into clay tablets in ancient Sumer more than 5,000 years ago?
Why did the coming of farming make cities possible?
items.a: It produced a food surplus, so people could settle in one place and some could do work other than growing food

ideas.title: Rome and its successors
ideas.summary: Rome's western half fell in 476; its eastern half lasted as the Byzantine Empire until 1453.

items.q: In what year does the Western Roman Empire traditionally end, when its last emperor was deposed?
Which city did the emperor Constantine make the new capital of the Roman Empire in 330?
What name is given to the Eastern Roman Empire, which outlived the fall of Rome by nearly a thousand years?
In what year did Constantinople fall to the Ottoman Turks?

ideas.title: The printing press
ideas.summary: Movable type made books cheap and ideas fast, feeding the Renaissance, the Reformation and modern science.

items.q: Who introduced printing with movable metal type to Europe around 1450?
What was the first major book printed with movable type in Europe, completed in the 1450s?
In what year did Martin Luther publish his Ninety-five Theses, the event that began the Protestant Reformation?
How did the printing press change the spread of ideas in Europe?
items.a: Books and pamphlets became cheap and quick to copy, so ideas spread widely and were hard to suppress

ideas.title: The Columbian exchange
ideas.summary: After 1492, crops, animals, people and diseases crossed the Atlantic and remade both hemispheres.

items.q: In what year did Christopher Columbus first reach the Americas?
What is the Columbian exchange?
items.a: The transfer of plants, animals, people and diseases between the Americas and the Old World after 1492

items.q: Which Old World disease is most associated with the collapse of Native American populations after 1492?
Which staple crop from the Andes became a mainstay of the northern European diet after the Columbian exchange?

ideas.title: Revolution and industry
ideas.summary: From the 1770s, political revolutions turned subjects into citizens while steam and factories remade work.

items.q: In what year did the French Revolution begin with the storming of the Bastille?
Which revolution, won in 1804, founded the first nation created by formerly enslaved people?
In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin, in the second half of the 1700s?
Which Scottish engineer's improved steam engine, patented in 1769, became the workhorse of the Industrial Revolution?

ideas.title: The world wars
ideas.summary: Two wars between 1914 and 1945 broke the old European empires and led to the founding of the United Nations.

items.q: In what years did the First World War begin and end?
What event in Sarajevo in June 1914 set off the First World War?
items.a: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria

items.q: What event on 1 September 1939 began the Second World War in Europe?
Which international organization was founded in 1945, at the end of the Second World War, to keep the peace?
